fi-aulonocara-jacobfreibergi.title: Aulonocara jacobfreibergi
fi-aulonocara-jacobfreibergi.summary: The Malawi butterfly, Aulonocara jacobfreibergi, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, living where rocky shores give way to sand. One of the larger members of the genus, with males reaching 150 to…
rows: Endemic to Lake Malawi where it's known only from the southern portion of the lake with populations including Cape Maclear, Otter Point, Mumbo and Domwe Islands, Monkey Bay,…
notes: Arrange some piles of rockwork around the tank but leave some open spaces between them and use fine sand as substrate so that it's able to feed naturally (see 'diet').
Coarser options such as gravel or small pebbles can inhibit feeding, damage gill filaments and even be ingested with the potential of internal damage/blockages.

fi-maylandia-zebra.title: Maylandia zebra
fi-maylandia-zebra.summary: The zebra mbuna, Maylandia zebra, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, where it inhabits rocky zones around shores, reefs and islands. One of the more aggressive mbuna, it is not a fish for a general…
rows: It will accept most foods offered but as with most Mbuna vegetable matter should form the basis of the diet.
notes: Keep it in a typical Malawi setup, with much of the tank filled with piles of rock arranged to form lots of caves and crevices.

fi-dimidiochromis-compressiceps.title: Dimidiochromis compressiceps
fi-dimidiochromis-compressiceps.summary: The Malawi eye-biter, Dimidiochromis compressiceps, is a predatory cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, where it is widely distributed. An ambush predator, it hides head-down among Vallisneria beds, its…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. Will accept dried foods such as pellets but these should not form the basis of the diet.
Endemic to Lake Malawi, where it's widely distributed.
notes: Set up the aquarium with piles of rocks arranged to form caves, large areas of open water for swimming and preferably a sandy substrate.
Planting with Vallisneria in dense patches would simulate the natural habitat of the species.

fi-labidochromis-caeruleus.title: Electric Yellow Lab Cichlid
fi-labidochromis-caeruleus.summary: Labidochromis caeruleus is a relatively peaceful mbuna from the northern part of Lake Malawi, best known in the hobby for its 'electric yellow' morph. That morph is one of the rarer forms in nature,…
notes: Much of the aquarium should contain piles of rocks arranged to form caves with small areas of open water between.

fi-melanochromis-auratus.title: Auratus Cichlid
fi-melanochromis-auratus.summary: The golden mbuna, Melanochromis auratus, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, common down the western coast and along the southern end of the lake. One of the most aggressive and territorial mbuna,…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach etc.
notes: Much of the aquarium should contain piles of rocks arranged to form caves with small areas of open water between.
A sandy substrate is best and the water should be well oxygenated.

fi-otopharynx-lithobates.title: Otopharynx Lithobates Cichlid
fi-otopharynx-lithobates.summary: The sulphur-headed hap, Otopharynx lithobates, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, where it lives among caves and crevices in rocky areas. A true rock dweller, it is hardly ever seen in open water,…
notes: Much of the aquarium should contain piles of rocks, arranged to form caves with areas of open water between.

fi-pseudotropheus-socolofi.title: Socolofi Cichlid
fi-pseudotropheus-socolofi.summary: The powder blue cichlid, Pseudotropheus socolofi, is a mbuna endemic to Lake Malawi, found along the Mozambique coast between Cobue and Tumbi Point. Also known as 'Eduard's mbuna' and 'Pindani', it…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach, nori etc.
notes: Arrange piles of rockwork in such a way as to form lots of caves and hiding places, leaving some open areas for swimming.

fi-aulonocara-stuartgranti.title: Sunshine Peacock Cichlid
fi-aulonocara-stuartgranti.summary: Grant's peacock, Aulonocara stuartgranti, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, widely distributed along both the east and west coastlines. Males vary in colour by locality, with blue forms found…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Endemic to Lake Malawi, where it is widely-distributed along both east and west coastlines.
notes: Arrange some piles of rockwork around the aquarium, but leave some open spaces between them and use fine sand as substrate so that the fish are able to feed in a natural way (see 'Diet').
Coarser options such as gravel or small pebbles can inhibit feeding, damage gill filaments and even be ingested with the potential of internal damage/blockages.

fi-copadichromis-borleyi.title: Redfin Copadichromis Borleyi Cichlid
fi-copadichromis-borleyi.summary: Copadichromis borleyi is an Utaka cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, where it shoals over rocky areas and isolated boulders at 5-20 metres. One of the species most commonly encountered in the hobby, it…
rows: group of 3 or more females, so that no particular female is singled out for excessive male attention.
Copadichromis are specialised zooplankton feeders, although they usually prove to be unfussy in captivity.
notes: As it's an open water species it needs plenty of swimming space.

fi-cyrtocara-moorii.title: Albino Cyrtocara Moorii Cichlid
fi-cyrtocara-moorii.summary: The Malawi blue dolphin, Cyrtocara moorii, is a large, peaceful cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, found mainly over shallow sandy areas. Formerly named Haplochromis moorii, it shoals in nature and…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Predator / carnivore. It's a micro- predator by nature, so the bulk of the diet should be composed of live and frozen foods.
notes: Provide a substrate of sand and plenty of open swimming space.
Unless the tank is really huge it's best to restrict any rock work to the perimeters, as the species can be quite flighty and may injure itself in a rock-filled setup.

fi-fossorochromis-rostratus.title: Fossochromis Rostratus Cichlid
fi-fossorochromis-rostratus.summary: Fossorochromis rostratus is a large, sand-sifting cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, most common over shallow sandy substrates. When startled it may bury itself, and a sand substrate is essential since…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Unfussy but live and frozen foods should comprise a large proportion of the diet.
notes: Set up the aquarium with large piles of rocks arranged to form caves, large areas of open water for swimming and a sandy substrate.
We recommend restricting the rockwork to the edges of the aquarium as F.

fi-iodotropheus-sprengerae.title: Rusty Cichlid
fi-iodotropheus-sprengerae.summary: The rusty cichlid, Iodotropheus sprengerae, is a dwarf mbuna endemic to Lake Malawi, around the islands of Boadzulu, Chinyankwazi and Chinyamwezi. One of the least aggressive and smallest mbuna in…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
notes: Use sand as substrate and furnish the majority of the tank with piles of rock, arranged to form plenty of caves and hidey-holes.
Hard water tolerant plants such as Vallisneria or Anubias can be used, but aren't essential.

fi-maylandia-greshakei.title: Albino Ice Blue Redtop Zebra Cichlid
fi-maylandia-greshakei.summary: The red top ice blue zebra, Maylandia greshakei, is an mbuna endemic to Lake Malawi, found only around Makokola in the southeast of the lake. It inhabits the upper parts of rocky reefs next to open…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach etc.
notes: Much of the aquarium should contain piles of rocks, arranged to form caves with small areas of open water between.
A sandy substrate is best and the water should be well oxygenated.

fi-maylandia-lombardoi.title: Kenyi Maylandia Lombardoi Cichlid
fi-maylandia-lombardoi.summary: Known in the hobby as the kennyi, Pseudotropheus lombardoi is a mbuna endemic to Lake Malawi, confined to the Mbenji Islands and Nkhomo Reef. In a reverse of the usual mbuna pattern, dominant males…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach, nori etc.
notes: Much of the aquarium should contain piles of rocks arranged to form caves with small areas of open water between.

fi-melanochromis-cyaneorhabdos.title: Electric Blue Johanni Cichlid
fi-melanochromis-cyaneorhabdos.summary: Melanochromis cyaneorhabdos is an mbuna endemic to Lake Malawi, known from one locality on the northeastern shore of Likoma Island. Formerly known as M. 'maingano', it is sometimes incorrectly sold…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach etc.
notes: Much of the aquarium should contain piles of rocks, arranged to form caves with small areas of open water between.
A sandy substrate is best and the water should be well oxygenated.

fi-aulonocara-nyassae.title: Red Shoulder Peacock Cichlid
fi-aulonocara-nyassae.summary: The red shoulder peacock, Aulonocara hansbaenschi, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, known from four localities on its southeastern shore. Some authors regard it as a geographical variant of the…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Endemic to Lake Malawi where it's known from just four localities; Masinje (type locality), Fort Maguire, Mara Point and Thumbi West Island.
notes: Arrange some piles of rockwork around the tank but leave some open spaces between them and use fine sand as substrate so that it's able to feed naturally (see 'diet').
Coarser options such as gravel or small pebbles can inhibit feeding, damage gill filaments and even be ingested with the potential of internal damage/blockages.

fi-sciaenochromis-ahli.title: Electric Blue Ahli Cichlid
fi-sciaenochromis-ahli.summary: The electric blue hap, Sciaenochromis fryeri, is a non-mbuna cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, found along rocky shorelines and the sandy zones beyond. It was previously imported and classified as…
rows: A predatory species in nature, S.
notes: Form networks of caves using piles of rockwork in much of the aquarium, leaving some open areas for swimming.

fi-nimbochromis-venustus.title: Venustus Cichlid
fi-nimbochromis-venustus.summary: The venustus, Nimbochromis venustus, is a predatory cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, where it is fairly widespread. Also sold as 'giraffe hap' or 'giraffe cichlid' after its pattern of irregular dark…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Predator / carnivore. It is an exclusive piscivore in nature but there is no need to feed live fish in aquaria as it accepts dead foods readily.
notes: Set up the aquarium with piles of rocks arranged to form caves, large areas of open water for swimming and preferably a sandy substrate.

fi-placidochromis-electra.title: Deepwater Placidochromis Electra Cichlid
fi-placidochromis-electra.summary: The deepwater hap, Placidochromis electra, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, living over sandy bottoms usually below 7 metres. In nature it feeds on invertebrates stirred up by digging substrate…
rows: It will accept most foods offered.
notes: Decorate the tank with piles of rocks arranged to form caves and hiding places but leave open areas of substrate between these.

fi-placidochromis-milomo.title: VC-10 Placidochromis Milomo Cichlid
fi-placidochromis-milomo.summary: The Super VC 10 hap, Placidochromis milomo, is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, found in the southern part of the lake and at Nkhata Bay. Wild fish have massively enlarged lips for scraping algae…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
It will accept most live, frozen and dried foods.
notes: The aquarium should contain rock piles forming caves and hiding places with open areas between for swimming.

fi-protomelas-taeniolatus.title: Red Empress Cichlid
fi-protomelas-taeniolatus.summary: Protomelas taeniolatus is a cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, where it is widespread over rocky areas of shallow, clear water. Very similar to P. fenestratus, it is one of the more popular Protomelas,…
rows: Herbivore / algae browser. It feeds mainly on algae and other microrganisms in nature and requires a high fibre diet in the aquarium.
notes: Use piles of rocks to form lots of caves and hiding places with areas of open space for swimming between.

fi-pseudotropheus-demasoni.title: Pseudotropheus Demasoni Cichlid
fi-pseudotropheus-demasoni.summary: Pseudotropheus demasoni is a dwarf mbuna endemic to Lake Malawi, where it occurs around Pombo Rocks off the Tanzanian coast. It hugs rock surfaces more than most mbuna and is often seen swimming on…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach, nori etc.
notes: Create a network of caves and hiding places in the aquarium using piles of rockwork.
This species does not require a lot of open swimming space, preferring to hug rock surfaces, so much of the aquarium should be decorated in this way.

fi-pseudotropheus-elongatus.title: Pseudotropheus Elongatus Cichlid
fi-pseudotropheus-elongatus.summary: The elongate mbuna, Pseudotropheus elongatus, is a slender cichlid endemic to Lake Malawi, found in Mbamba Bay and Nkata Bay. Over 30 different forms occur in the lake and they hybridise freely, so…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach, nori etc.
notes: Use piles of rocks to form cave-like structures and hiding places, leaving areas of open water for swimming.

fi-melanochromis-joanjohnsonae.title: Exasperatus Cichlid
fi-melanochromis-joanjohnsonae.summary: The pearl of Likoma ( Labidochromis joanjohnsonae) is a species of fish in the family Cichlidae endemic to Lake Malawi where it is native to rocky areas around Likoma Island and it has been…
rows: Up to about 10.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-pseudotropheus-crabro.title: Bumblebee Maylandia Ornatus Cichlid
fi-pseudotropheus-crabro.summary: Freshwater invertebrate: Bumblebee Maylandia Ornatus Cichlid (Pseudotropheus crabro).
rows: Up to about 9.4 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-copadichromis-mloto.title: Ivory Head Copadichromis Mloto Cichlid
fi-copadichromis-mloto.summary: Copadichromis mloto is a species of haplochromine cichlid which is endemic to Lake Malawi.
rows: Up to about 13.5 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-buccochromis-nototaenia.title: Stripeback Hap (Buccochromis nototaenia)
fi-buccochromis-nototaenia.summary: A fast, open-water predatory cichlid from Lake Malawi that hunts young fish over sand near the shore. Rare in the trade because it is hard to catch.
rows: 48 × 18 in footprint (about 64 gal) as a bare minimum; it needs lots of swimming room
Not very aggressive toward fish too big to swallow, but small fish will be eaten. Suits larger Malawi species (over about 6 in), not mbuna
Tolerates its own kind well in a roomy tank
Predator that adapts to prepared foods: a cichlid pellet staple plus meaty foods such as prawn and mussel. Greedy, so do not overfeed
Endemic to Lake Malawi (also Lake Malombe): Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania
notes: Excellent filtration and regular maintenance are essential for such a large, heavily fed fish.
Rocks are optional; open swimming space matters most.

fi-melanochromis-chipokae.title: Chipokae Cichlid
fi-melanochromis-chipokae.summary: A striped, predatory mbuna known only from one reef near Chipoka Island in Lake Malawi. Among the most aggressive mbuna and not for beginners; it is Critically Endangered in the wild.
rows: Very aggressive and territorial; a dominant male usually rules the tank. Keep only with similar-sized robust mbuna that look different
Seriously Fish suggests stocking mbuna tanks heavily to spread aggression and adding this species last
Omnivore: varied live, frozen and dried foods, with spirulina or other vegetable foods as a supplement
Lake Malawi: only around Chindunga Rocks, off Chipoka in the south-west of the lake
notes: Fill much of the tank with piled rock forming caves, over sand, with good oxygenation.

fi-protomelas-fenestratus.title: Fenestratus Cichlid
fi-protomelas-fenestratus.summary: A gentle Lake Malawi hap that blows sand off rocks to uncover small prey. Males turn blue over a window-like barred pattern. It suits peacock-type communities, not rowdy mbuna.
rows: Peaceful for a Malawi cichlid, but territorial when breeding; males fight each other
One male with several females; a very large tank is needed for more than one male
Takes most foods, but live and frozen foods should make up most of the diet
Lake Malawi (northern and south-western parts), along rocky shores and the sand just beyond
notes: Rock piles with caves and open sand between them.
Do not keep with Protomelas taeniolatus or similar Protomelas, as they may hybridise. Good tankmates: Aulonocara, Copadichromis and other peaceful Malawi species.

fi-nimbochromis-livingstonii.title: Livingstonii Cichlid (Livingston's Cichlid)
fi-nimbochromis-livingstonii.summary: A blotched ambush predator from Lake Malawi that lies still on the bottom as if dead, then grabs small fish that come close. Locally called 'kalingono' (sleeper).
rows: 48 × 18 in footprint (about 54 gal) as a minimum; larger is better for a predator this size
Predatory but generally peaceful with fish too large to eat; smaller mbuna and young fish will be eaten
A loner: keep one, or one male with several females for breeding
Fish-eater in the wild, but takes dead meaty foods (prawn, lancefish, whitebait). No mammal meat
Lake Malawi (fairly widespread), the upper Shire River and Lake Malombe; inshore areas over sand
notes: Rock caves plus large open swimming areas over sand; dense patches of Vallisneria mimic its habitat. Keep the current gentle.
Not a fish for a general Malawi community. Suits large Rift Lake fish such as frontosa or large mbuna.

fi-maylandia-estherae.title: Red Zebra Cichlid
fi-maylandia-estherae.sci: Maylandia estherae (sometimes listed as M. zebra)
fi-maylandia-estherae.summary: A Lake Malawi rock-dwelling mbuna, best known in its orange-red form. It was split from Maylandia zebra as its own species in 1995 and is still often sold as Pseudotropheus or Metriaclima estherae.
rows: Males about 5 in (135 mm SL; Wikipedia gives 12.7 cm), females about 4 in (10 cm); FishBase lists 7.9 cm SL
Fairly mild for a mbuna but still robust; keep with similar-sized mbuna, not with peacocks or other gentle haps
One male with several females; a well-stocked rock tank spreads out aggression
Mostly plant matter: spirulina flake, nori, blanched spinach and similar, with some live or frozen foods. Feed small amounts; it gets fat easily. Never feed beef heart or other mammal meat
Endemic to Lake Malawi, along the rocky Mozambique and Malawi shores near Metangula
notes: Build piles of rock with caves over sand and let algae grow on the rocks for grazing.
Color varies by sex and locality: males are often blue and females orange, and orange and orange-blotched ("OB") forms exist.
It will cross with related mbuna, so do not keep different color forms or close relatives together if you want pure fish.
A mouthbrooder: females carry the eggs and fry for about three weeks.
